extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: A large-scale open-source multimodal interleaved pre-training dataset containing one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images sourced from HTML, PDFs, and ArXiv documents.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.citeAs: Awadalla, Anas, et al. MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271v5, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built from CommonCrawl HTML and PDF dumps and ArXiv LaTeX sources. HTML documents were extracted from CommonCrawl WARC files by parsing each WARC entry's DOM tree. PDF documents were sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files by extracting PDF links, downloading PDFs, and reading them with PyMuPDF. ArXiv interleaved documents were built from LaTeX source code using TexSoup to find figure tags and interleave images with paper text. The data was filtered using rules-based heuristics, deduplication methods, safety filtering, and image filtering. No crowdworkers or contractors were involved; only the authors were involved.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from CommonCrawl WARC dumps for HTML documents, CommonCrawl WAT dumps for PDF links and PDFs, and ArXiv S3 buckets / LaTeX source code for ArXiv documents. For HTML documents the released data contains document text and image URLs. For PDFs and ArXiv, the released data contains text, the PDF URL, and image reference numbers used to parse images from the documents.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024. HTML documents were sourced from CommonCrawl dumps from May 2017 to April 2024, PDF documents from CommonCrawl dumps from February 2023 to April 2024, and the datasheet states the dataset includes web data from 2013 to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For PDFs, reading order was extracted by finding bounding boxes of text blocks on a page, clustering blocks based on columns, and ordering blocks from top left to bottom right. Images were anchored in sequence based on proximity between image bounding boxes and text blocks on the same page. For ArXiv, figure tags were identified from LaTeX, multi-file papers were merged by replacing input tags with file contents, and LaTeX imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags were removed. Personally identifiable information was anonymized by replacing email addresses with templates such as "email@example.com" and IP addresses with randomly generated non-functional IPs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included filtering out HTML documents with no images or more than thirty images and images with URLs containing inappropriate substrings such as logo, avatar, porn, and xxx. Non-English documents were removed using FastText language identification with a confidence threshold of 0.65. Documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings were removed. Text filtering from RefinedWeb was applied, removing documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or identified as low quality using MassiveText rules. For PDFs, documents larger than 50MB or over 50 pages were discarded, and pages with no text were excluded. Images were downloaded where possible; non-retrievable links were discarded and documents with no valid image links were removed. Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels were removed. HTML images with aspect ratio greater than two were removed; for PDFs the threshold was three. NSFW image detection was applied and any document containing a single NSFW image was discarded. Deduplication included paragraph and document text deduplication using a Bloom Filter with false positive rate 0.01 on 13-gram paragraphs, discarding documents where more than 80% of paragraphs were duplicates; exact paragraph deduplication on 2% of each CommonCrawl snapshot to remove boilerplate text; and image deduplication using SHA256 hashes, removing images appearing more than ten times within a snapshot and repeated images within a single document.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: FastText language identification model; NSFW image detector (GantMan/nsfw_model)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be released publicly through the Huggingface interface as JSON shards. The authors will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README in the Huggingface interface. An erratum will be present on the README of the Huggingface dataset page. Older versions can be found using the Git history of the dataset repository, and issues with previous versions will be communicated in the erratum. The authors will accept contributions through the Pull Request mechanism of the Huggingface interface. The datasheet states the dataset will be updated by the authors and that a DOI will be provided when released.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper states that because the dataset is sourced from the public web, it may contain images of individuals, text about specific individuals, confidential content, and sensitive data present on the public web, including data that may reveal race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, locations, financial or health data, biometric or genetic data, government identification, or criminal history. The dataset may also contain personally identifiable information, though email addresses and IP addresses are masked.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that MINT-1T is intended to make research into large multimodal models more accessible and be a valuable resource for the research community to do open science on multimodal interleaved datasets. It also notes the importance of avoiding exposure of harmful content from the web and says future work should explore more ways to improve the safety of multimodal internet data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that OBELICS shows a pronounced concentration in Humanities and Social Sciences, while MINT-1T's HTML subset is not strongly biased towards any specific domain and the PDF subset has a higher proportion of Science and Technology documents. In the datasheet, the authors state they follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models because such models have been shown to favor text from certain demographics, and they encourage consumers to further filter the data based on their use case.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in PDF parsing: PyMuPDF sometimes fails to detect images, and because PDFs have arbitrary layouts, the extracted reading order can be incorrect, including reading across column boundaries or starting from the rightmost column. This is described as a compromise between speed and accuracy. The dataset is not self-contained and relies on external image URLs, with no guarantees that URLs will remain available over time due to link rot; the full dataset with images is infeasible to host because it is over 300TB. The paper also notes that harmful, offensive, confidential, or sensitive content may still be present despite filtering. Non-recommended uses include training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information, such as images of people's faces and other sensitive content, as well as military applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset was built for pre-training large multimodal models that process multiple interleaved images and text. The datasheet states there is only a training split for MINT-1T. It has already been used to train large multimodal models to validate data quality against competitors. The paper also states it could be used for other training objectives like generating interleaved images and text sequences or building multimodal document retrieval systems. The dataset is designated primarily as a research artifact, and users are responsible for ensuring legal use in commercial settings.
